donor_structure: Neutral networks: the set of genotypes folding to one phenotype forms connected components under point mutations; mutational robustness = average node degree; a population drifts along the component; network topology (connectivity, degree distribution) predicts evolvability and accessibility of adjacent phenotypes.
target_structure: metric on H (inherited structure / inheritance channel) under which 'nearby inheritance' is meaningful: two inheritance records are near if one can be obtained from the other by burden-neutral elementary inheritance events; R4 needs this for archive/novelty decisions over H.
mapping: genotype -> inheritance record (strategy/module/constitution fragment); point mutation -> elementary inheritance event (copy, edit, drop); phenotype -> realized function/behaviour; neutral network component -> burden-neutral inheritance class; mutational robustness -> inheritance robustness (number of neutral variants of an H); phenotype adjacency -> reachable innovation step.
preserved_relations: connectivity of neutral classes: neutral inheritance sets are connected under elementary events (under the analogue conditions that hold in GP maps)
robustness-evolvability correlation: high neutrality grants access to more distinct neighbours (innovation through drift on the component)
metric reading: edit distance on H restricted to a neutral class stays at 0 burden change - 'nearby inheritance' = short path in the event graph
